title: The local engine forces --lowvram on every NVIDIA GPU - is that costing users real speed?
description: routes/comfy.js launches ComfyUI with --lowvram for every detected NVIDIA GPU, unconditionally, regardless of card size or model size. The user's authoring bench (G:\ComfyUiun_nvidia_gpu.bat) passes no VRAM flag at all, so it runs ComfyUI's default NORMAL_VRAM. That is the one unconditional difference between where his fast H3 runs happened and where the slow ones happen, and it matches the reported symptom exactly: dedicated VRAM parks at 11.5 of 16GB while 23.7GB spills to shared - 'like having a 10GB card when I have 16'. NOT proven. The app's own log for 2026-08-07 shows 6.4, 10.2, 23.5, 47.5, 94 and 143 s/it, so settings dominate and the app is not uniformly slow. One isolation test decides it (see brief.md). If it wins, the fix is CONDITIONAL, never a deletion - --lowvram was added deliberately (MPI-142/143/144: default normalvram OOM-killed a 42GB LTX transformer on a 24GB 4090) - and it must sweep BOTH engine twins, routes/comfy.js and routes/remotePodLifecycle.js.
